headline: Generals charged at last; MACC's procurement probe spans 4,600-plus projects
context: Former Army Chief Hafizuddeain Jantan and former Defence Forces Chief Mohamad Nizam Jaafar were charged with corruption in January 2026 and pleaded not guilty. MACC is also examining 158 large and more than 4,500 smaller defence projects.

changes.summary: Correction: An earlier edition attributed a co-accused spouse to the wrong general; that line is removed. The cartel is now described as suspected and its 4,600-plus projects as under investigation, and figures with no source (RM52 million seized, 12 auditors, RM6.1 billion) are removed.

cards.big: Two former military chiefs were charged with corruption in January 2026. Both pleaded not guilty. The bigger test is the procurement system around them.
cards.sub: By 30 January, Hafizuddeain faced six money-laundering charges; Nizam faced four abuse-of-power counts and a CBT count involving RM3 million.

cards.big: A suspected 26-firm cartel allegedly bribed senior officers for military contracts, GlobalPost reported in January 2026.
cards.sub: MACC is examining 158 projects above RM500,000 and more than 4,500 smaller ones. By 30 January the probe had led to 23 arrests.

cards.big: The LCS warship scandal's CBT case against a former navy chief ended in a DNAA in March 2025. Ten months later, a suspected 26-firm cartel surfaced.
cards.sub: A Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court found Ahmad Ramli Nor unfit for trial on three CBT counts involving RM21.08 million.

cards.big: Opening Parliament on 19 January 2026, the King warned of a wider hunt for the corrupt: 'I will continue to hunt you down.'
cards.sub: The first general was charged three days later. Each charge remains an allegation until a court rules on it.

cards.big: Two prosecutions test two men. A suspected 26-firm cartel tests the procurement system itself. The LCS case, ended by a DNAA, shows how such tests can stall.
The charges matter. But soldiers deserve more than the trial of two generals. They deserve a procurement system that cannot be captured.
